title: JWT session cache key collision causing cross-org authz exposure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers reported intermittent privilege escalation where API calls authenticated with a valid JWT from Org A were authorized as if they belonged to Org B. Root cause appears to be a session/JWT cache key omission in our edge proxy layer causing cache entries to be looked up without org scoping under specific load/burst patterns.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use two org accounts (Org-A and Org-B) with similar user ids.
2) Rapidly issue token refresh flows from both orgs through same edge gateway behind burst routing.
3) Observe that a subset of requests for Org-A return cached session metadata with org_id=Org-B when edge proxy cache key prunes tenant namespace under high QPS.
4) Confirm by inspecting gateway cache keys and auth logs tracing correlation-id.
impact_summary: Customer escalations from 3 enterprise accounts (Hosted + two Dedicated tenants). Symptoms: incorrect organization-scoped metadata returned (org_id mismatch), resulting in read access to some resources across org boundaries. No evidence of write operations executed across orgs so far, but read-level data exposure is unacceptable and classified as high customer impact.
investigation_notes: - SLO/alerts: spike in 401/403 anomalies and increased rate of org-scoped permission checks failing then passing when retried.

- Edge proxy (v2.7.3) cache key construction omitted the org_id when the incoming Authorization header was a short-lived JWT and the proxy used a normalized cache path for token introspection results.

- Race condition: when concurrent refresh requests arrive, token introspection result is written with key 'introspect:<kid>:user:<uid>' instead of 'introspect:<org_id>:<kid>:user:<uid>' resulting in collisions across orgs with the same uid/kid pattern.

- Seen primarily when routing policy sent requests to same edge instance for both hosted and dedicated backends (burst routing path). Dedicated instances using per-tenant virtual host usually unaffected unless behind shared gateway.
- Relevant logs: gateway-introspect.log correlated by request_id: https://logs.company/internal/gateway-introspect/2026-03-12/trace-7f3b (ACL redacted link shared with customer under NDA).
- Reproduction validated in staging by simulating two tenants with same user id and sending 2k parallel refresh requests; collision rate ~0.7%.
- No database corruption found. Token revocation flows unaffected.
mitigation: Short-term (hotfix): deploy proxy image 2.7.4 with org_id included in cache key generation and set cache TTL to 30s for introspection results to force fresh validation during rollout.
Customer remediation: rotate affected API keys/JWTs for the three impacted customers and export audit logs. Offer one-on-one support and 72-hour monitoring window.
Traffic control: enable canary routing to route suspected noisy clients to a dedicated proxy pool until fix is verified.
Communications: incident email drafted and sent to CSMs for impacted customers; case numbers recorded.
Monitoring: added Prometheus metric gateway_introspect_cache_misses_tagged_by_org and alert when cross-org mismatch rate >0.1%.
root_cause: Edge gateway cache key construction omitted org scoping in token introspection cache under a legacy normalization codepath. This interacts with burst routing where multiple tenants share the same proxy instance and user id/KID collisions occur.
plan: 1) Merge hotfix PR to add org_id into cache key and short TTL + run full unit/integration tests (auth, introspect, routing).
2) Run load test in staging reproducer to ensure collision rate <0.001% at 10k RPS mixed-tenant traffic.
3) Gradual rollout: deploy to 10% of edge fleet, monitor for errors for 2 hours, then 50%, then 100%.
4) Post-deploy: rotate affected tokens with customer opt-in; offer forensic audit exports.
5) Retrospective: update design doc, add automated regression test to CI, and update playbook.
6) Long-term: refactor cache key builder to be explicitly tenant-first and add static analysis rule to prevent future omissions.
acceptance_criteria: - Hotfix landed and deployed to edge fleet with org-scoped cache key.
- Staging reproducer shows collision rate reduced to indistinguishable from zero under targeted load.
- No additional customer reports of cross-org reads for 7 days after full rollout.
- CI contains a regression test that simulates multi-tenant concurrent refresh flows.
- Security review completed and customers notified with remediation steps.
related_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/2317 (add integration test for tenant-scoped introspect cache)
